claim: Added hook time can be repaid only where the original wastes some: a delay the game pads with, a fixed-length uncontended copy, the game's own long routine at 28 MHz, or a plot after the game's sync.

evidence.text: The game pads each pass with (10 - figures) delay calls; repaying to the T-state gave +0.1% against +2.1% without.
The update delay scales with droid count and vanishes at 6 or more blocks, so hook time must be repaid.
Pace was won by running the game's own 21 ms scroll at 28 MHz (down to 4 ms).
Every plot follows the game's own sync (a HALT); added time near the frame's end went past the sync.
A game that waits for FRAMES needs no limiter round its plots.
